      "observations": [
        "Read all 1,227 owned diff lines across 28 Thunderbird/shared paths, including all 130 new test lines and the 121-line generated operation. Product/directive preflight found no Suite section. Generated output is functional and was inspected for request construction and type behavior; its style is not guidance. Exact accepted ancestry and NUL paths match.",
        "The Graph operation adds /me/messages/{message-id}/$value to supported_paths, exports the generated module and calls its Get constructor. The generated path trims the endpoint slash, inserts the ID, uses GET and an empty body, and declares Vec<u8>. Generated documentation instead says Get open extension and labels PUT/DELETE as eventMessage; these labels do not describe the literal media path. They must not replace request-code evidence or authorize editing generated output.",
        "The client splits raw send_request from send_request_json_response. The raw helper still builds/authenticates/sends, checks client/server HTTP errors and returns the Response; the JSON helper alone substitutes null for empty bytes and invokes serde_json. Existing create/send/folder-delta/message-delta operations switch to the JSON helper, while get_message forwards response.body() directly. Current queue/options/batching and base_api_url are later phases, not original transport credit.",
        "The new XPCOM get_message implementation replaces NotImplemented: it obtains initialized details, wraps the fetch listener, copies the ID and detaches the local async task, then returns Ok. Actual data follows on_fetch_start, request completion and on_fetched_data_available. Generic DoOperation owns the success/error completion path, and the safe fetch listener maps both outcomes to onFetchStop. Reuse the existing completion lesson; synchronous start acceptance is not network completion.",
        "The native changes preserve three URI roles: graph folder URIs, graph-message URIs containing the local message key, and x-moz-graph channel URIs. Folder base URI construction chooses the graph root, service conversion moves the fragment into the channel path while preserving query, header lookup maps back to graph, and AsyncOpen selects the graph message service. EWS mappings remain. Accepted files use Exchange* names; current GetUrlForUri additionally passes through an existing x-moz channel URI, a later change.",
        "Component registration declares Graph message-service aliases and a separate protocol constructor/configuration with internal flags. Preferences add internal expose/external values, the extension MESSAGE_PROTOCOLS list adds x-moz-graph, and AttachmentInfo adds it to the normal non-feed URL regex. The current extension consumer still checks its actual permissions and the attachment consumer has earlier URL/feed/UNC branches. These comm declarations do not establish paired Gecko protocol registration, clickable-link security or every attachment/extension path at runtime.",
        "The fake Graph GET branch matches the URL-safe ID character class and writes MIME content directly rather than serializing JSON. Its original nullable media helper returns null for an absent item or absent syntheticMessage, but the original route immediately reads content.length without a null guard. The added positive test does not cover either missing-media branch. Current fake code later returns HttpResponseData and uses a different response path; no current HTTP status or reproduced server failure is inferred.",
        "MockServer.addMessages now mutates each input SyntheticMessage.messageId after base64 encoding, replacing the first + and / and replacing final padding with its count. Tests consequently pass the mutated IDs rather than btoa(original). The new raw-content expectation calls toMessageString after this mutation, matching the fake body producer. These are test-model identifiers, not a production RFC Message-ID migration. The replacement calls are non-global; repeated occurrences are not normalized by those calls, and no fixture demonstrating that boundary was executed.",
        "The new test initializes both EWS and Graph clients, syncs their root/folder state and fetches two generated messages per protocol. It directly asserts the folder count and fetched content; it does not exercise the channel/offline-store handoff, rendering, cancellation, unknown IDs, callback failure or multiple data events. Its listener overwrites _data on each callback; the inspected Rust operation delivers one full response body, so this is a single-delivery test rather than demonstrated multi-chunk accumulation.",
        "The new content assertion Assert.equal(data, messages[i].toMessageString()) has no message argument. The folder-count assertion has a nonempty should message. The missing message is one changed lexical site used by both protocol tasks; unrelated unchanged assertions in adjacent tests are outside this finding. No test code or messages were written.",
        "The generated UserSelection/getter/setter addition for identityParentId follows the existing absence/null/type distinction and warns that setter presence does not guarantee Graph writability. It is generated schema output incidental to regeneration, not a fetch response field or a live-service compatibility result. Header line wrapping and adjacent C++ formatting changes are mechanical within the functional patch; no global style rule follows.",
        "Manual readability/comment review: the raw/JSON split and early returns keep distinct completion roles visible; the comment explaining the non-JSON mock response gives a useful reason. The original EwsService channel comment names only x-moz-ews although its code also maps Graph; current comment later names both. Placeholder docs and the ID helper claim need the exact source limits above. No request, server, stream, UI, lint, native build or runtime test was executed.",
        "Complete primary 2018995 current comments 0–7, activity and footer were read from exact A original 0fc66916207c044616567012ba8d18aae345317147992a9603b2d0d4275c7ea5. It separately records upstream x-moz-graph protocol and comm message-fetch landings. Comments 5–6 name D292900 and report a rebase behind Bug 2030283; keep those actual labels without inferring an engine/source pairing or a runtime result.",
        "Complete retained D291020 includes all five actual inline bodies, including the older generator thread at diff 1244335. Owned source adopts the comment naming both internal schemes, URL-safe mock-ID regex/conversion and supported_paths.txt entry. The regex request is qualified and the external Microsoft rules remain unopened; local code, including its non-global replacements, is the adoption evidence.",
        "The reviewer requests a logging-related rebase; the final owned generator input is in supported_paths.txt. The earlier author hopes a component detail can be removed before landing; no removal is inferred from that hope. Later native renamed files, queue transport, base URL helper and HttpResponseData fake are comparison phases, not original credits.",
        "Reviewer says confirmed it works for me and the author supplies Try links after acceptance; those are historical attributed reports. Own review approval, Done flags, build messages and the primary closure do not establish fresh Graph service, MIME display, offline store, cancellation or native integration success.",
        "Source review keeps the new byte-comparison missing-message site, positive-only listener test, synthetic ID mutation and original mock null-length boundary explicit. No test, request, benchmark, native build, lint or rendered UI action ran."
